terra.problem: The final sentence is a flat, circular observation: the age matters because it is the age at which the story happens.
The yearly trips were made by Jesus' parents. The passage does not establish that Jesus had visited Jerusalem before.
Luke 3:23 says Jesus was about thirty, not simply thirty, when He began His ministry.
The passage says His parents were unaware He had stayed and assumed He was in their company. It does not say they thought everything was fine.
A walk down a line of people is an invented detail about how the search happened.
The text does not say they walked back or how long the return took.
Anxiously searching does not establish that they never sat still.
The passage says they found Him after three days, but does not say their search lasted three days.
It presents three days as the duration of the search, which the passage does not specify.
The explanation repeatedly restates where Jesus was found without adding a meaningful observation or Papa Dorin's personality.
Luke says Jesus was sitting among the teachers, not that the teachers themselves were sitting.
The description of the Mount of Olives as a hill near Jerusalem is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
Saying listening and asking is all the text says overlooks His answers in the next verse.
The passage also mentions Jesus' answers, so listening and asking are not all it tells us about what He was doing.
The text does not establish that Jesus was not up front leading anything.
The text says all who heard Him were astounded. It does not say anyone walked away.
Calling puzzled close to the mood adds a reaction the text does not give.
The watch line invents details about what the listeners did and presents them as fact.
The closing line calls the statement worth slowing down for but offers no observation about it, leaving the explanation generic.
The text says His parents did not understand His statement, but does not specify that they heard every word.
The explanation repeats the answer and adds only a generic observation about the story winding down.
The explanation repeats the same fact throughout without adding a meaningful observation or Papa Dorin's personality.
Saying she did not forget any of it goes beyond the statement that she treasured these things in her heart.
The claim that Jews and Greeks are paired elsewhere in the New Testament needs a reference.
